intro: Kyle Thomas, a Vermont glam-garage musician.
story: King Tuff is Kyle Thomas, a Vermont musician who played in Feathers, Happy Birthday and Witch before taking the name and has been active since 2006. Black Moon Spell, his third album, came out September 23, 2014 on Sub Pop, produced by Bobby Harlow, and NPR called it the sound of one guy making sure everyone has a good time. He played Pickathon in 2013 and 2015. The Other followed in 2018 and Smalltown Stardust in 2023, in gentler psych-folk textures.
artist_reel_line: Smalltown Stardust, in 2023, brought gentler psych-folk textures.

story: Rodrigo Amarante was born in Rio de Janeiro in 1976 and joined the Brazilian rock band Los Hermanos around its 1999 debut; he also played in Orquestra Imperial and Little Joy. His solo debut, Cavalo, came out in Brazil in late 2013 and worldwide in 2014 on Polyvinyl, and ranked sixth on Rolling Stone Brasil's best national albums of 2013. He played Pickathon in 2015, the year his song Tuyo became the theme of Netflix's Narcos. Drama followed in 2021.
artist_reel_line: Tuyo became the Narcos theme in 2015; Drama followed in 2021.

story: Sonny & the Sunsets is the San Francisco project of Sonny Smith, who is also a playwright and an artist, with a sound that ranges from garage and doo wop to country. Longtime Companion, on Polyvinyl on June 26, 2012, was his first country record, recorded straight to tape in a basement. His 100 Records project invented 100 fictional bands, each with album art by an artist and songs recorded for the imagined records, and Pitchfork said the final volume, in January 2013, was much stronger than it had any right to be. The band played Pickathon in 2011, 2012 and 2015. Smith keeps working between music, plays and visual art.
artist_reel_line: Smith moves between music, plays and visual art; 100 Records invented 100 fictional bands.

story: Viet Cong formed in Calgary in 2012 around the bassist Matt Flegel and the drummer Mike Wallace, formerly of the band Women, with the guitarists Scott Munro and Daniel Christiansen. Their self-titled debut came out January 20, 2015 on Flemish Eye and Jagjaguwar, Pitchfork named it Best New Music, and it was a Polaris Prize nominee. They played Pickathon that year. In April 2016 they renamed themselves Preoccupations after a Pitchfork interview and released a self-titled album in September, then New Material in 2018, Arrangements in 2022 and Ill At Ease. Flegel described Monotony as a dead-end job and Anxiety as changing as a band.
artist_reel_line: As Preoccupations, they released Ill At Ease and toured Europe and North America.
